01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Paul Tol color palette and dual-layer sparkline table (gray=full dataset, indigo=selection) show real design intent, but the dense line tangle in the parallel coordinates reduces readability without interaction.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.encoding_integrity_note: Structurally honest — parallel coord y-scales use data-driven d3.extent(), sparkline histograms lock to global maxCount for consistent before/after comparison, no area deception — but histogram threshold is a hardcoded magic number (24) instead of Sturges'/Scott's rule, and fg-bars data join lacks a key function.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.stress_test_note: The expensive canvas redraw and table DOM mutations are properly RAF-coalesced via a dirty-flag pattern, but drawStrums() executes a raw D3 data join and DOM mutation on every pointermove without RAF throttling; all other checks pass cleanly — no transitions to interrupt, no cross-view dispatch loops, scales are stable (no resize handler), and the Pointer Events API with setPointerCapture eliminates mouse/touch double-fire.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.cognitive_load_note: 2 linked views, 6 well-chosen colors, and smart alpha layering (0.06 unselected / 0.55 selected) keep the architecture sound, but the default all-150-lines state renders as a dense rainbow tangle that demands interaction before structure emerges.
